title: ModelProfilesArtifact
description: Versioned output of the calibration stage (pipeline-python). Written to artifacts/model-profiles.json. Supplies predicted_error[model, cluster] to the routing formula. Cross-field invariants this schema cannot express on its own (every cluster id must exist in the referenced cluster map's 0..k-1 range; number_succeeded + number_failed must equal number_of_tasks; raw/smoothed rates must be consistent with the counts) are enforced by pipeline-python's profiles.py at write time, and must be re-checked by any consumer before trusting the file.

artifact_id.description: Stable identifier for this calibration build, e.g. 'profiles-2026-08-06-a'.

cluster_map_id.description: Must equal the artifact_id of the cluster-map.json these profiles were calibrated against. This linkage is what makes cluster id 7 mean the same thing in both files; a mismatch means the error table is silently permuted relative to the centroids, so consumers MUST hard-fail on a mismatch rather than degrade.

cluster_map_digest.description: Optional SHA-256 over the cluster-map.json bytes, for detecting a map edited in place without an artifact_id bump.

cluster_count.description: The k of the referenced cluster map, copied here so coverage gaps are checkable without loading the map.

embedding.description: Must match the referenced cluster map's embedding block — calibration tasks are assigned to clusters using this model, so a mismatch invalidates every assignment.

smoothing.description: Descriptive metadata for auditors. The runtime reads the stored smoothed_error_rate and NEVER recomputes it — that is what makes a routing decision reproducible from this artifact alone.

task_selection.description: How the calibration task pool was chosen, for reproducibility.

models.description: One entry per calibrated candidate. Identity is model_id; duplicates are rejected at write time. Onboarding a new model appends an entry here and bumps artifact_id — the cluster map is untouched.

runner.description: How this candidate produced solutions. 'reference' and 'null' are grader-validation controls, not real models — consumers should exclude them from routing candidate sets.

is_control.description: True for grader-validation controls (reference/null). A router must never select a control as a real candidate.

calibration_run_id.description: Identifies the measurement conditions (harness version, tools, prompt). Re-running calibration after changing the agent harness must produce a new run id — the numbers only describe the model+harness combination they were measured under.

clusters.description: Keyed by cluster id as a decimal string. Lookup only, never iterated by the runtime. A missing cluster key means no calibration coverage there; the runtime falls back to `global` and logs the degradation.

profileStats.description: number_of_tasks counts ONLY graded pass/fail outcomes. Tasks excluded for environment reasons (missing dependency, timeout, harness error) are tallied separately in `excluded` and deliberately kept out of the denominator — a slow machine or a missing library must never be recorded as a model failure.

excluded.description: Outcomes kept out of the error-rate denominator. Present so a thin or environment-blocked cluster is visible rather than mistaken for a confident rate.
